subject: Poppr amova issue with subsetting variance among pop, among samples within pop, and within sample

messages.author: 4dc47c156cad1815
messages.subject: Poppr amova issue with subsetting variance among pop, among samples within pop, and within sample
parts:
Hello,
I am having trouble pulling up the value of within population variation in my AMOVA. I am sure this is an easy fix but I am new at this so not sure what I am doing wrong

>vcf <- read.vcfR("new_ref_mc_noclones.vcf.gz")
>popdata<-read.table("popmap_noclones_vcf", sep = "\t")
>colnames(popdata)<-c("sample","pop")

 head(popdata)
  
sample               pop
1   ind0 BancoDeSanAntonio
2   ind1 BancoDeSanAntonio
3   ind2    Guanahacabibes
4   ind3    Guanahacabibes
5   ind4    Guanahacabibes
6   ind5    Guanahacabibes

>cuba.genind <- vcfR2genind(vcf)
>cuba.genclone <- poppr::as.genclone(cuba.genind)
>strata(cuba.genclone) <- data.frame(popdata)
>setPop(cuba.genclone)<-~pop

This is a genclone object
-------------------------
Genotype information:

     79 original multilocus genotypes 
     79 diploid individuals
   9531 codominant loci

Population information:

      2 strata - sample, pop
      8 populations defined - BancoDeSanAntonio, Guanahacabibes, IslaDeJuventud, ..., CaboLucrecia, CayoSabinal, CayoJutias


>amova <- poppr.amova(cuba.genclone, ~pop)

$call
ade4::amova(samples = xtab, distances = xdist, structures = xstruct)

$results
                Df    Sum Sq  Mean Sq
Between samples  7  12038.19 1719.742
Within samples  71  90481.95 1274.394
Total           78 102520.14 1314.361

$componentsofcovariance
                                 Sigma          %
Variations  Between samples   46.69656   3.534699
Variations  Within samples  1274.39360  96.465301
Total variations            1321.09016 100.000000

$statphi
                         Phi
Phi-samples-total 0.03534699

Why is it not subsetting variation among populations, among samples within populations, and within samples?
Any help would be greatly appreciated!

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Poppr amova issue with subsetting variance among pop, among samples within pop, and within sample
parts:
Hello Alexis,

This is a bit odd indeed. The default of poppr.amova() is to automatically calculate within-individual variance. I suspect it has something to do with the fact that vcfR only exports its alleles as zeroes and ones. Would you be willing to (privately) send me a copy of your data so that I can try to reproduce this?

In the meantime, one other thing you might try if you have a compiler on your computer is to use the development version of vcfR (remotes::install_github("knausb/vcfR")) and use vcfR2genind(vcf, return.alleles = TRUE).

Let me know if that helps.

Best,
Zhian

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Poppr amova issue with subsetting variance among pop, among samples within pop, and within sample
parts:
An additional note for folks in general with vcf data:

If you only have bi-allelic SNPs, then you should use vcfR2genlight(), the time difference in conversion and calculating AMOVA is MUCH faster:

print(system.time(genind_numeric <- vcfR2genind(vcf)))
#    user  system elapsed
#  41.466   0.012  41.478
print(system.time(genind_character <- vcfR2genind(vcf, return.alleles = TRUE)))
#    user  system elapsed
#  45.778   0.020  45.814
print(system.time(genlight_vcf <- vcfR2genlight(vcf)))
#    user  system elapsed
#   0.515   0.000   0.516

parts:
Hello Zhian,
I had the same problem and I have gendid object, converted from Data Set of Bialellic SNPS, I had the same issue "not calculating the within population in the Anova)



This is what I used

poppr.amova(GS.Object.4Amova, hier = ~Pop/Pop_Sub, clonecorrect = FALSE, within = F,
            dist = NULL, freq = TRUE,
            correction = "quasieuclid",  filter = T,
            threshold = 0, algorithm = "average_neighbor",
            missing = "loci", cutoff = 0.05, quiet = FALSE,
            method = "pegas", nperm = 2)


Second.Amova <- poppr.amova(GS.Object.4Amova, hier = ~Pop, clonecorrect = FALSE, within = T,
            dist = NULL, freq = TRUE,
            correction = "quasieuclid",  filter = T,
            threshold = 0, algorithm = "farthest_neighbor",
            missing = "loci", cutoff = 0.05, quiet = FALSE,
            method = c("ade4","pegas"), nperm = 2)

Any hint is appreciated.
Thanks so much,
Nelly

Can you confirm that you have a genlight object and not genind?

On Wednesday, December 11, 2019 at 5:43:16 AM UTC-5, Zhian Kamvar wrote:
An additional note for folks in general with vcf data:

If you only have bi-allelic SNPs, then you should use vcfR2genlight(), the time difference in conversion and calculating AMOVA is MUCH faster:

print(system.time(genind_numeric <- vcfR2genind(vcf)))
#    user  system elapsed
#  41.466   0.012  41.478
print(system.time(genind_character <- vcfR2genind(vcf, return.alleles = TRUE)))
#    user  system elapsed
#  45.778   0.020  45.814
print(system.time(genlight_vcf <- vcfR2genlight(vcf)))
#    user  system elapsed
#   0.515   0.000   0.516

On Mon, Dec 9, 2019 at 7:54 PM 'Alexis Sturm' via poppr <po...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
Your suggestions actually worked! Thanks so much Zhian!

On Monday, December 9, 2019 at 4:51:03 AM UTC-5, Zhian Kamvar wrote:
Hello Alexis,

This is a bit odd indeed. The default of poppr.amova() is to automatically calculate within-individual variance. I suspect it has something to do with the fact that vcfR only exports its alleles as zeroes and ones. Would you be willing to (privately) send me a copy of your data so that I can try to reproduce this?

In the meantime, one other thing you might try if you have a compiler on your computer is to use the development version of vcfR (remotes::install_github("knausb/vcfR")) and use vcfR2genind(vcf, return.alleles = TRUE).

Let me know if that helps.

Best,
Zhian
